LEARNING PATH LESSON · SIGHT WORDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

And — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

Five minutes, one card: you will chain two favourites together: socks and shoes, bread and butter, up and down, and your child will meet “and” in a real sentence, “Mum and Dad” By the end, “and” should be a word they know at a glance.

What is this?

“And” is a joining and turning word. On this card, a boy and a girl stand side by side with a small & sign between them, with the word printed in big, clear letters underneath.

What does it mean?

“And” links or turns ideas around, as in “Mum and Dad”

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs to recognise “and” at a glance, say it clearly, and begin to hear it in the stories you read together. Good hunting grounds: pairs everywhere: salt and pepper, knife and fork, you and me.

Why this matters

Joining words like “and” let a child move from single words to whole thoughts, which is exactly what early reading asks for.

What it teaches

Linking two ideas, early sentence building and recognition of a very common word.

Words to learn

wordreadjoin

Say this to your child

“Look at this card. It says ‘and’. Mum and Dad Now you say ‘and’. Well done!”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and read “and” clearly, running your finger under the letters. Let your child say it back, twice.
  2. Look at the picture together: a boy and a girl stand side by side with a small & sign between them. Ask what is happening, then link the picture to the word.
  3. Play one tiny game: chain two favourites together: socks and shoes, bread and butter, up and down. Read the word one last time and stop while it is still fun.

Look closer at the picture

Point to the word first, then to the picture. Cover the picture with your hand and read the word; lift your hand to check. Then let your child trace the first letter with one finger.

Ask your child

“What does the card say?” “Can you make a sentence with “and”?” “What is happening in the picture?” — answered with a read-aloud and a silly sentence.

What your child can say or do

Expect longer sentences than usual, with “and” doing the joining.

Out in the real world

Watch for “and” here: pairs everywhere: salt and pepper, knife and fork, you and me. Every sighting is a free practice round: point, say it, move on.

Try it together

Chain two favourites together: socks and shoes, bread and butter, up and down. Finish by saying “and” one more time.

Understanding check

Tomorrow, hold up the card without saying a word. If your child reads “and” straight away, the word has arrived; if not, play the game once more and try again the day after.

Parent tips

If “and” does not stick today, do not push. Slip the card into tomorrow’s pile and try again with a smile.

This lesson pairs with the And flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sight Words (Class 29).
